newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures shave gains late, end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures shave gains late, end higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures shaved gains late and ended surprisingly light trading moderately higher.

Traders said the December Treasury bond futures pared its large gains into the close on scattered, moderate-size dealer selling that drew other closing long liquidation when the contract slipped back below the 106-31/32 level.
They noted a lack of followthrough, especially on the downside, in both the long and short ends on surprisingly low turnover, given the broad width of day's ranges.
"The Street's complacent. There's no followthrough," noted one Eurodollar floor broker before the close.
They tied much of the day's gains to shortcovering after the early kneejerk selloff on August U.S. employment figures ran out of power, sending shorts scrambling.
"They were all dressed up, hunting bear this morning, and they just couldn't get them down," said another Eurodollar floor broker of the market's swift break and rebound.
"There was definitely selling on the number, but as soon as they had any way of assessing what the market was doing, (it) was seven or eight ticks higher," said a third broker.
Nonfarm jobs rose 250,000, near forecasts, but joblessness slid to 5.1 percent and hourly wages jumped by six cents.
Opinions continued to diverge about the likelihood and extent of a Federal Reserve rate hike late this month after the employment figures.
Some said the short end at the morning's early lows had priced in at least 50 basis points of tightening but by day's end had factored out roughly half of that.
"If the Fed hikes 25 basis points, December (Euros) has already priced it in," said the first Euro broker.
In the long end, prices spent the afternoon gradually grinding higher as some shorts capitulated, and December T-bonds occasionally hit small buystops.
But brokers said the advance never gained full power, which persuaded some day-longs to bail out near the close.

During the morning's fall, December T-bonds put in a spike low at 105-09/32, which it never reapproached. It subsequently clawed its way above minor resistance zones, including 106-20/32, 106-25/32 and Thursday's high at 107-02/32.

Some traders, however, looked for a resumption of choppy range-trading nearterm before prices back down again, with a couple of chartists foreseeing a break back below support at the June 13 low of 104-31/32 in December T-bonds and longerterm a slide toward par.

December T-bonds ended up 11/32 at 106-24/32, T-notes gained 11/32 to 105-23/32, muni-bonds added 22/32 to 111-14/32, December Eurodollars gained seven basis points to 93.92, and T-bills gained eight basis points to 94.53. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
